transcript.answer: No, not any more. ADR-039 originally decided that review-type agents should run on a different model family from the implementer. The idea was to pin the review default to another family, such as OpenAI's flagship when the implementer is Claude. The settings UI would warn when both resolved to the same family. An amendment dated 2026-10-14 reversed this. `code-review` and `code-review-recheck` now run on `gemini-4-argon`, the same family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. `code-review-reply` stays on `claude-sonnet-4-6`. The amendment says cross-family review "is no longer a rule, only one input to the model choice." Its reason is that in a local bench, Argon found all five of the finished must-fixes with no false alarms, against four of six for Sonnet. The catch rate outweighed the self-preference risk. The cost is that Argon is about 3x slower and about 40% dearer. Same-family review is allowed. The earlier warning helpers from PR #1091 still exist as an advisory.

judgements.reason: The answer says cross-family review is no longer required, notes that ADR-039 originally made it the rule, and states that the 2026-10-14 amendment moved code-review and code-review-recheck to gemini-4-argon, the implementer's family, because it caught more, leaving cross-family as only one input.
